current_definition: Useful or effective for a particular immediate purpose, but often chosen for convenience or self-interest rather than for principled reasons.
To make a process or task happen more quickly than it would under normal conditions; to speed it up.
(Of a plan, effort, or organisation) to fail completely, especially after a promising start.
To put a plan, policy, or decision into practical effect; to actually carry it out.
A supposed remedy or solution claimed to fix all problems at once; a cure-all that rarely delivers in practice.
Focused on practical results and what actually works in the real world, rather than on theory, ideology, or rigid principles.
To formally and publicly take back a belief, statement, or accusation that one previously held or made, often under pressure or in light of new evidence.
To formally give up a right, title, claim, or privilege, usually in a public and permanent way.
Designed to be useful and practical rather than beautiful or decorative; concerned with producing the most benefit for the greatest number of people.
The period of European history from the 14th to the 16th century, marked by a great flowering of art, science, and learning.
A departure from what is normal or expected, especially one that is unwanted or suggests something has gone wrong.
The most perfect or typical example of a kind of person or thing; an original model that others seem to copy.
Made up of parts or elements that are so different from one another that they seem to have nothing in common.
Drawing from a wide variety of sources, styles, or ideas rather than following a single approach.
The natural force that pulls objects toward one another, keeping planets in orbit and feet on the ground.
A small place, group, or system that contains, in miniature, all the features and complexities of something much larger.
A young person who has an extraordinary natural talent that far exceeds what is normal for their age.
To restrict or limit the range, freedom, or power of something or someone.
Matching in size, degree, or importance; in proportion to something else.
Sharing a border or touching at the edge; directly next to or connected with something.
To describe, mark out, or explain something precisely and in clear detail.
Individually separate and distinct; existing as a clearly defined unit rather than blending into a whole.
Made up of parts or members that are all of the same kind or very similar to one another.
The outer edge or boundary of an area, group, or subject; the part furthest from the centre.
To prevent something from happening or to make it impossible in advance.
The state of being near or close to someone or something in space, time, or relationship.
To isolate or set apart a person, group, or thing from outside contact or influence.
Effectively the same as something else; equal to something in value, meaning, or effect.
The same throughout; not varying in form, quality, or degree from one part or instance to another.
To shorten a piece of writing or speech by cutting parts out while keeping the essential meaning.
To set aside or distribute a resource, such as money, space, or time, for a particular purpose or person.
A material made by combining two or more metals, or a metal and another element, to produce a substance with improved qualities.
Extremely small; so tiny that it is almost impossible to measure or notice.
Necessary to make something complete; forming an essential part of a whole rather than being optional or additional.

Required by a particular situation or purpose; necessary as a condition before something can happen or be accepted.
At the most basic or early stage of development; involving only the simplest skills, knowledge, or features.

Likely to cause disagreement or argument; also describes a person who enjoys arguing or picking fights.

So bad or wrong that it stands out clearly and shocks people; much worse than ordinary mistakes.
To make a bad situation or problem even worse, often when it was already serious.
To irritate or frustrate a person so much that they feel they have completely run out of patience.

Persistently unlucky; describes someone who seems to attract misfortune without doing anything to deserve it.
Moving or progressing in a very slow, heavy, and labored way; also describes speech or writing that feels unnecessarily long and dull.
To make something last much longer than it needs to or should, often causing frustration.
To prevent someone from making progress or achieving a goal; to block or obstruct completely.
The habit of caring about others and acting to help them, with no expectation of getting anything back. A truly altruistic act costs the giver something and benefits someone else entirely.
